info.name: Blu Mountain HubSpot MCP Server
info.description:
This service's own exposed HTTP endpoints (not HubSpot's API directly) — /install, /callback, /health, /, the two webhook receivers, and the API-key-gated debug HubSpot data API (gateway/debug_api.py). Excludes /install/mcp-auth and /callback/mcp-auth (removed in the REST pivot, openspec/changes/hubspot-rest-api-pivot) and the /mcp mount (MCP protocol over Streamable HTTP, not a plain REST endpoint Postman represents naturally — use MCP Inspector instead, see CLAUDE.md's Development commands).

Uses the {{base_url}} collection variable, defaulting to http://localhost:8888 (docker compose up's dev stack). The two webhook requests carry a pre-request script that computes a real, valid signature from a collection variable holding the relevant secret, so they run against a live server exactly as HubSpot/Sybill would call them — not just a URL list.

To actually pull real HubSpot data: set {{debug_api_key}} to match the server's own DEBUG_API_KEY, run 'List installed tenants' (its test script auto-fills {{hub_id}} from the first result), then run any of the requests under 'Debug: HubSpot Data' — they all use {{hub_id}}.

variable.description: The running mcp-gateway service. docker compose up's dev stack serves this on :8888 by default.
Optional human-readable name for /install's ?portal_name= param. HubSpot has no API for this — whoever sends the install link supplies it.

Must match SYBILL_WEBHOOK in the server's own .env for the pre-request script's computed signature to verify. The whsec_ prefix is optional — verify_svix_signature strips it either way. Replace with the real value to test against a real deployment; this default matches the test suite's own dummy secret, not a real Sybill secret.
Must match HUBSPOT_APP_CLIENT_SECRET in the server's own .env for the uninstall webhook's computed signature to verify. Replace with the real value to test against a real deployment.
A hub_id already present in the tenants table (from a completed /install) — the uninstall webhook example targets this one. Change to whichever real or test tenant you want to exercise.

Must match the running server's own DEBUG_API_KEY (see .env.example). Every /debug/hubspot/* request 401s without this — empty by default so a fresh import can't accidentally reach real tenant data with no setup.

Which installed tenant the Debug: HubSpot Data requests pull from. Run 'List installed tenants' first — its test script fills this in automatically from the first tenant returned — or set it by hand to a specific hub_id.

Which custom object 'Pull a custom object's records' reads. Run 'List custom object schemas' first — its test script fills this in automatically from the first schema returned — or set it by hand to a real objectTypeId (e.g. 2-3465404).

request.description: Reflects real service state: Postgres connectivity and scheduler status. Returns {"status": "healthy"|"degraded", "postgres": "connected"|"unreachable", "scheduler": "running"|"stopped"}.

Lists this service's active route groups (active_paths) — a quick sanity check that expected subsystems are mounted (hubspot-oauth, token-vault, airtable-staging, sybill-ingestion, live-mcp-session). Should NOT list mcp-auth — that was removed in the REST pivot.

Starts the OAuth v3 + PKCE install flow: redirects (307) to HubSpot's own authorization screen, listing every scope in HUBSPOT_SCOPES (required) plus whichever of HUBSPOT_OPTIONAL_SCOPES the connecting portal's tier supports. This is the single onboarding step — the MCP Auth App's second install step no longer exists.

Postman follows redirects by default; to inspect the raw 307 and its Location header (the actual HubSpot authorize URL, useful for confirming exactly which scopes are being requested under scope= vs optional_scope=), turn off 'Automatically follow redirects' in this request's Settings tab, or in the collection's global settings.

exec: pm.test('redirects toward HubSpot (or 200 if redirects were followed)', () => {

request.description: In real use, HubSpot itself redirects a portal admin's browser here with ?code=...&state=... after they approve the install — this endpoint isn't meaningfully callable standalone from Postman with a fabricated code/state (the state must match a real oauth_states row created by a real /install call in the same browser session, and the code must be a real HubSpot-issued authorization code). Calling it bare, as this request does, exercises the 'missing required information' error path (400) and its styled HTML error page — a genuine, useful smoke test in its own right.

exec: pm.test('renders the styled HTML error page, not raw JSON', () => {

request.description:
Sybill call-transcript webhook, Svix-signed (svix-id/svix-timestamp/svix-signature headers, HMAC-SHA256). This request's pre-request script computes a real, valid signature from {{sybill_webhook_secret}} — no manual header-crafting needed, but the secret variable must match the server's own SYBILL_WEBHOOK for it to verify.

Tenant resolution reads data.crm.{id,type} against hubspot_object_index (populated by real staged Company/Deal pulls) — replace REPLACE_WITH_A_REAL_INDEXED_OBJECT_ID with a real hs_object_id already staged for a connected tenant, or this returns 422 (tenant not resolvable), which is itself a valid, informative response confirming signature verification passed but no matching tenant exists. crm.type accepts 'deal'/'opportunity' or 'company'/'account' (Sybill uses Salesforce-flavored terms; HubSpot's own terms are also accepted).

request.description:
HubSpot's app-lifecycle uninstall webhook (X-HubSpot-Signature-V3 + X-HubSpot-Request-Timestamp headers, plain HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the raw body). This request's pre-request script computes a real, valid signature from {{hubspot_app_client_secret}} — must match the server's own HUBSPOT_APP_CLIENT_SECRET to verify.

CAUTION: a real, valid call against a real portalId genuinely invalidates that tenant's vaulted token and marks it uninstalled (auth/token_vault.py::hubspot_uninstall_webhook) — this is a real, not read-only, action against whichever {{test_hub_id}} you point it at. Use a disposable test tenant, not a real client's hub_id, unless you specifically intend to uninstall it.

item.name: Debug: HubSpot Data (test accounts)
item.description:
gateway/debug_api.py — a plain HTTP surface for pulling a real installed tenant's HubSpot data directly, since the /mcp mount is MCP protocol, not something Postman can call naturally. Gated by {{debug_api_key}} (X-Debug-Api-Key header) — every request 401s if it's unset or wrong, matching the server's own DEBUG_API_KEY. Every successful pull is recorded in this project's own audit_log, same as any other HubSpot access path. Read-only, same guarantee as every other path in this project.

Workflow: run 'List installed tenants' first (fills {{hub_id}} automatically from the first result), then run any request below.

request.description: Every currently-installed tenant, with its display name. Run this first — its test script below fills {{hub_id}} in automatically from the first tenant returned, so every other request in this folder is ready to run immediately after.
The fixed set of valid {object_type} and {capability_name} path segments the requests below accept — useful reference, not tenant-specific.

Real contacts for {{hub_id}} via GET /crm/v3/objects/contacts. Add ?properties=email,jobtitle to narrow the response to exact HubSpot property names instead of the default set (REST's properties= is exclusive, not additive).
Real companies for {{hub_id}} via GET /crm/v3/objects/companies.
Real deals for {{hub_id}} via GET /crm/v3/objects/deals.
Real line items (LINE_ITEM) for {{hub_id}} via GET /crm/v3/objects/line_items.
Real products (PRODUCT) for {{hub_id}} via GET /crm/v3/objects/products.
Real CRM users (USER) for {{hub_id}} via GET /crm/v3/objects/users.
Real quotes (QUOTE) for {{hub_id}} via GET /crm/v3/objects/quotes.
Real email engagements (EMAIL) for {{hub_id}} via GET /crm/v3/objects/emails.

Change the last path segment to any CRM object type or alias this project supports (tickets, line_items, products, calls, emails, meetings, notes, tasks, users, campaign, landing_pages, blog_posts, lists — see 'List object types & capabilities'). Aliases like plurals/irregular forms are accepted (e.g. 'companies', 'meetings').

exec: pm.test('200 OK or a clear 400 for a bad type', () => pm.expect([200, 400]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: Every real property HubSpot has for this object type on this tenant's portal, including custom ones, with HubSpot's own authoritative hubspotDefined flag (true = standard, false = custom). Change the last path segment to any CRM object type/alias.
Change the last path segment to any capability from 'List object types & capabilities' (owners, organization_details, content_analytics, marketing_email_analytics, campaign_attribution).

Every custom object schema defined on {{hub_id}}'s real portal, discovered fresh (openspec/changes/custom-object-support) — there's no fixed list of these the way there is for standard object types. Returns an empty list (not an error) on a portal without Custom Objects access, an Enterprise-tier HubSpot feature. Run this first — its test script fills {{custom_object_type_id}} in automatically from the first schema returned.

Real records for one custom object, by its objectTypeId — run 'List custom object schemas' first to populate {{custom_object_type_id}}. Add ?properties=field1,field2 to narrow the response, same as the standard-object pull requests above.

Per-campaign attribution metrics for {{hub_id}} — enumerates real campaigns, then pulls each one's metrics. Returns an empty list (not an error) on a portal without Marketing Hub Professional+, since marketing.campaigns.read is an optional OAuth scope for exactly that reason.
